extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examination guidance for (1) use and identification of trade names/trademarks in patent applications, (2) inclusion and authorization of copyright or mask-work notices, and (3) required form, content, and standards for drawings submitted with patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper identification of product/service/organization when using marks
rubrics_metrics.description: If proper identification of the product, service, or organization identified by a mark or trade name is omitted from the specification and such identification is deemed necessary, the examiner should hold the disclosure insufficient and reject claims based on identification merely by mark or trade name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a product cannot otherwise be defined, an amendment defining the process of its manufacture may be permitted unless such amendment would introduce new matter; such amendments must be supported by satisfactory showings establishing the specific nature or process of manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect proprietary nature of marks used in commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Although use of marks having definite meanings is permissible in patent applications, the proprietary nature of marks should be respected; marks should be identified by capitalizing each letter (for word/letter marks) or otherwise indicating the mark's description (for symbols/devices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every effort should be made to prevent use in any manner that might adversely affect their validity as commercial marks. Examiners may search the Trademark Electronic Search System (TESS) to determine whether a mark is registered or what goods it applies to. Use form paragraph 6.20 to inform applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.20 guidance for marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a trade name or mark in the application should be accompanied by generic terminology and capitalized or include proper symbol (™, SM, ®).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Para 6.20 text: inform applicant to accompany the term with generic terminology and capitalize or include symbol. Examiner Notes: (1) Capitalize each letter of the term or include proper commerce symbol. (2) Examiners may use TESS to search for registered marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid language that obscures trade/mark status
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not permit phrasing like 'product X (a descriptive name) commonly known as Y (trade name or mark)' since it fails to clearly indicate Y is a trade name or mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible phrasing: 'product X (a descriptive name) sold under the trademark Y.' Also avoid using marks in the title or coupling a mark with the word 'type' (e.g., 'Band-Aid type bandage').

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of registered marks depicted in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered mark is a 'symbol or device' depicted in a drawing, either the brief description of the drawing or the detailed description should specify that the symbol/device is a registered mark of the identified company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The owner of a mark may be identified in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling complaints regarding misuse of marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Technology Center Directors should reply to complaint letters about misuse of marks and forward copies of the complaint and reply to the Office of the Deputy Commissioner for Patent Examination Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a letter shows misuse in a patent application publication and the application is still pending, the Office should ensure replacement of the mark with appropriate generic terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission and content limits for copyright/mask work notices
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in a design or utility patent application adjacent to the protected material, but the content of the notice must be limited to only those elements provided for by law (e.g., '©1983 John Doe' or '*M* John Doe').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion is permitted only if the authorization language set forth in 37 CFR 1.71(e) is included at the beginning (preferably first paragraph) of the specification to be printed for the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization statement required for inclusion of notices (§1.71(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The inclusion of a copyright or mask work notice will be permitted only if the specification includes the required authorization language (the authorization paragraph specified in §1.71(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorization must state that a portion of the disclosure contains material subject to copyright/mask work and that the owner has no objection to facsimile reproduction by anyone of the patent document as it appears in the PTO files, but otherwise reserves all rights. If absent or altered, the notice will be objected to as improper and petitionable under 37 CFR 1.181.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright/mask work notice placement and size in drawings (§1.84(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice placed in a drawing must be within sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the protected material and limited to letters .32 cm to .64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content must be legally limited (examples provided). Inclusion after a Notice of Allowance is permitted only if criteria of 37 CFR 1.312 are satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for permitting copyright or mask work notices (A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of such notices is permitted only if: (A) notice placed adjacent to material (and if in drawing must comply with §1.84(s)); (B) content limited to elements required by law; (C) the authorization of §1.71(e) included at the beginning of the specification; and (D) inclusion after Notice of Allowance obeys 37 CFR 1.312.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departure from these conditions may result in refusal; if the authorization language does not include specific wording about facsimile reproduction, the notice will be objected to; examiner objections may be petitioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to furnish drawings where necessary (37 CFR 1.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is required to furnish a drawing of the invention where necessary for understanding the subject matter sought to be patented; the applicant should retain original drawings for corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may include illustrations facilitating understanding (e.g., flow sheets for processes, diagrammatic views). Corrections are applicant responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner requirement when subject admits illustration but none furnished (37 CFR 1.81(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the nature of the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and the applicant has not furnished such a drawing, the examiner will require its submission and give at least two months for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings submitted after filing may not be used to overcome insufficiency or to supplement original disclosure for claim interpretation; requirement should be clearly indicated as under 37 CFR 1.81(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings submitted after filing cannot cure insufficiency or supplement disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted after the filing date may not be used (i) to overcome any insufficiency of the specification due to lack of enabling disclosure or (ii) to supplement the original disclosure for purpose of interpreting claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should include necessary drawings at filing when required; late drawings may be limited in use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules for drawings (pre- and post-December 18, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on/after Dec 18, 2013 (except design apps), 35 U.S.C. 111 no longer requires a drawing for a filing date; 35 U.S.C. 113 still requires drawings where necessary. For design applications, a required drawing must be filed to obtain a filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-PLT (before Dec 18, 2013) applications, a drawing or high-quality copy was required where necessary; OPAP determines if a drawing is necessary for filing date. Inclusion of drawings with provisional or nonprovisional filings is prudent to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim types where a drawing is not required for filing date (pre-PLT examples A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-PLT applications, a drawing is not required for a filing date if the application contains certain claim types, including: (A) at least one process claim using 'process' or 'method'; (B) at least one composition claim using 'composition', 'compound', 'mixture', or 'pharmaceutical'; (C) claims to coated articles or articles made from a particular material where article is conventional; (D) claims to laminated articles of conventional character; (E) claims to articles/apparatus where sole distinguishing feature is presence of a particular material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §601.01(f) and §601.01(g) for more complete explanation regarding when a drawing is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling substitute/additional drawings that introduce new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner discovers new matter in a substitute or additional drawing, the drawing should not be entered and the examiner should describe the new matter that resulted in non-entry in the next Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new drawing without new matter may be required if needed under 37 CFR 1.81 or 1.83. The decision not to enter a drawing is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181; TC Director decides such petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.23: requirement when subject admits illustration
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 6.23 notifies applicant that the subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and requires applicant to furnish a drawing under 37 CFR 1.81(c); no new matter may be introduced in the required drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requiring drawings before examination, use form paragraph 6.23.01 with a PTOL-90 or PTO-90C form as cover sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 6.23.01: shortened period and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 6.23.01 requires a drawing under 37 CFR 1.81 and gives applicant a shortened statutory period of TWO (2) MONTHS to submit the drawing; extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) may be obtained but cannot extend beyond six months total; failure to timely submit results in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-90/PTO-90C when requiring drawings; when requiring drawings before examination, include an ink sketch or permanent print as part of the next reply to show no new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black and white ink requirement for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required for utility and design patent applications; India ink or equivalent that secures solid black lines must be used for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs are not ordinarily permitted except where they are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and photographs: permitted conditions and petition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings permitted in design applications; color drawings in utility applications are accepted only on petition showing necessity, payment of fee, submission of required sets (1 set if filed electronically, 3 sets otherwise), and an amendment inserting specific language into the brief description of drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings must be of sufficient quality to be reproducible in black and white. Color drawings are not permitted in PCT international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). Color photographs accepted only if they meet same reproducibility and necessity conditions; photographs are acceptable for certain biological or structural images (e.g., gels, microscopy, animals, plants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia (title of invention, inventor's name, application number or docket number) should be provided on the front of each sheet within the top margin; each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked-up copies of amended drawing figures with annotations must be labeled 'Annotated Sheet' per §1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings (formulae, tables, waveforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements; each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure (using brackets when necessary); waveforms presented as a single figure with a common vertical axis and time along horizontal axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper quality and usage for drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper that is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable; all sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, folds, erasures, alterations, overwritings, and interlineations; only one side of the sheet may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the same sheet-size and margin requirements; see paragraph (b) for other photograph requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable drawing sheet sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size; acceptable sizes are 21.0 cm x 29.7 cm (A4) or 21.6 cm x 27.9 cm (8½ x 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the shorter sides of the sheet is regarded as its top.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margin requirements and sight area limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each sheet must include top margin ≥2.5 cm (1 inch), left margin ≥2.5 cm (1 inch), right margin ≥1.5 cm (5/8 inch), and bottom margin ≥1.0 cm (3/8 inch), leaving a sight no greater than specified depending on sheet size; sheets should have scan target points printed on two cater-corner margin corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views: number, arrangement, and separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention; views (plan, elevation, section, perspective) must be grouped together, arranged without wasting space, clearly separated, and not included on sheets with specifications/claims/abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Detail views and exploded views rules apply (exploded views embraced by bracket; place in brackets when on same sheet as another figure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views and linking across sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Large machines/devices may be broken into partial views on a single sheet or over several sheets as long as there's no loss in understanding; partial views on separate sheets must be linkable edge to edge with a smaller-scale view showing the whole and indicating positions of parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a view is enlarged for magnification, the main and enlarged views must each be labeled as separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional views and hatching conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional views must indicate the plane of the section on the view from which the section is taken by a broken line, designate ends with numerals corresponding to sectional view, and use arrows to indicate direction. Hatching must be regularly spaced oblique parallel lines (preferably 45°) spaced to be distinguishable and not impede reference characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break hatching where reference characters are inserted; parts in cross section must show proper materials by hatching; juxtaposed different elements must be hatched with different angled patterns; for large areas, hatching may be confined to edging drawn around the inside of the outline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions and modified forms depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A moved/alternate position may be shown by a broken line superimposed on a view if not crowding; otherwise a separate view must be used. Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exploded view is on same sheet as another figure, place exploded view in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement and orientation of views on sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another; all views on same sheet should stand in the same direction and, if possible, be readable with the sheet held upright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If very wide views are necessary, the sheet may be turned so top margin is on right-hand side. Words must appear left-to-right horizontally except for standard scientific graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the drawing views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may suggest a single figure number for front page inclusion. Views must not contain projection lines or center lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale limitations and prohibition of scale statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when reduced to two-thirds in reproduction. Indications like 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted because they lose meaning on reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose scale to preserve clarity after reprographic reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Lines, numbers, and letters must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined; weight of lines/letters must permit adequate reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement applies to all lines including fine lines and shading; different line thicknesses are allowed where they convey different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; shading indicates surface/shape of spherical, cylindrical, conical elements and may be used for flat parts; spaced thin lines preferred; solid black shading not permitted except for bar graphs or color.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As substitute for shading, heavy lines on shade side can be used where they do not obscure reference characters. Light should come from upper left at 45°.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbols in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate; elements represented by such symbols must be adequately identified in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Known devices should use universally recognized symbols; other symbols not universally recognized may be used subject to Office approval if not likely to be confused with existing symbols and are readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends: descriptive legends subject to approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used in drawings subject to Office approval or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters, letters, and numbers rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible, not used with brackets or inverted commas or enclosed outlines, and oriented in same direction as the view to avoid rotating the sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English alphabet must be used for letters except where another alphabet is customary (e.g., Greek). Numbers/letters/reference characters must be at least .32 cm (1/8 inch) in height; they should not interfere with comprehension, should not be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces (except underlining with blank space in hatching where necessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of reference characters across figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The same part of an invention appearing in more than one figure should be identified by the same reference character throughout the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent numbering aids comprehension and cross-reference between views (text at end of chunk begins this rule).
